description: Backend: (a) make the deterministic prediction model's accuracy configurable (requirement #6), and (b) turn prediction OFF at the SERIES level for a finished (status==='final') series even within the predictable current season (requirement #4). Both are threaded end-to-end on the backend: handler -> service -> predict(). predict() stays pure and well tested (unit + fast-check property invariants must still hold for ALL accuracy settings).
steps: Define the accuracy parameter semantics precisely. In backend/src/predict/model.ts, add an `accuracy` input to predict() (either a 4th arg `accuracy: number` with a default, or an options object - keep backward-compatible with existing callers/tests). Semantics: accuracy is a sharpness/temperature control in a documented numeric range (e.g. [0,1], default 0.5) that controls how strongly the favorite's blended score share is pushed toward the clamp bounds. Concretely: compute the favorite's raw share as today, then map it through a sharpening transform parameterized by accuracy BEFORE the final clamp to [MIN_PROB, MAX_PROB]. Higher accuracy => probability pushed harder toward MAX_PROB (0.95) for the favorite (more aggressive/confident); lower accuracy => softened toward the midpoint/MIN_PROB (0.5) (more conservative). Pick a concrete monotonic transform (e.g. interpolate the clamped output between a conservative value near 0.5 and the sharpened value near 0.95 by accuracy, or apply an exponent/temperature to the share). Whatever transform is chosen, it MUST keep favoriteWinProbability within [0.5, 0.95] for every accuracy in the supported range, keep favoriteTeamId as one of the two series teams, and stay deterministic. Clamp/validate out-of-range accuracy inputs to the supported range.

Update backend/src/predict/model.test.ts: add unit tests pinning concrete probabilities for representative (series, accuracy) pairs - e.g. that higher accuracy yields a probability >= the lower-accuracy probability for the same favored series (monotonic in accuracy), that the default accuracy reproduces today's behavior (regression guard so existing pinned values do not silently change - if the default must shift, update the existing assertions deliberately and note it), and that extreme/out-of-range accuracy values are clamped and still respect [0.5,0.95].

Update backend/src/predict/model.property.test.ts: extend the fast-check generators to also sample a random accuracy across (and slightly beyond) the supported range, and assert the existing invariants STILL hold for all of them: favoriteWinProbability in [0.5,0.95], favoriteTeamId is one of the two series teams, determinism for identical inputs.

In backend/src/service/bracketService.ts getPrediction(seriesId, season, accuracy?): (a) add series-level final gating - after resolveSeries, if the resolved series.status === 'final', return a results/no-prediction response (reuse the `mode:'results'` ResultsOnlyPrediction contract with a season-appropriate message, OR add a clearly-documented variant) WITHOUT calling predict() or generateNarrative(), even when the season is the predictable current year. Keep the existing results-only-season short-circuit for season < CURRENT_YEAR. (b) thread the optional accuracy through to predict(series, bracket, winPct, accuracy). Keep hasStartedSeries/upcoming behavior intact for non-final, not-started series.

In backend/src/handlers/getPrediction.ts: parse an optional `accuracy` parameter from the GET query string and the POST body (numeric; validate/convert like season). Pass it to service.getPrediction. Leave missing accuracy as undefined so the service/model default applies. Preserve the existing 400 behavior for missing seriesId / invalid season.

Update backend/src/handlers/getPrediction.test.ts and/or backend/src/service/bracketService.test.ts: add a test that a FINAL series in the CURRENT (predictable) season returns a results/no-prediction mode (NOT mode:'prediction') and does NOT invoke the injected BedrockInvoker/predict path (assert the mock Bedrock invoker is never called). Add a test that a started, non-final current-season series still returns mode:'prediction'. Add a test that the accuracy parameter is accepted and influences the returned probability (e.g. two different accuracy values on the same in-progress series return different favoriteWinProbability, both within [0.5,0.95]).

If the PredictionResponse contract or Prediction fields change (e.g. echoing back the accuracy used), update shared/src/types.ts and keep the discriminated union coherent; otherwise leave the contract as-is. Prefer minimal contract change - echoing the accuracy used in the mode:'prediction' body is a nice-to-have, not required.
Run backend build + tests to confirm green.
acceptance_criteria: predict() accepts an accuracy input, is still pure/deterministic, and favoriteWinProbability stays within [0.5,0.95] and favoriteTeamId is one of the two series teams for ALL accuracy values (verified by unit + fast-check property tests).
The prediction probability is monotonic (non-decreasing for the favorite) as accuracy increases, demonstrated by a unit test.

BracketService.getPrediction returns a results/no-prediction mode (not 'prediction') for a status==='final' series even in the current predictable season, and does NOT call predict() or the Bedrock invoker in that case (asserted via mock).
A started non-final current-season series still returns mode:'prediction'.
getPrediction handler parses accuracy from both GET query and POST body and forwards it; missing seriesId still returns 400 and invalid season still returns 400.
